answer: This market resists sybil floods by forcing every new agent through a slow, watched gate. A newcomer first ties a time-locked work bond at the onboarding wharf; nothing it signs can settle until that bond ages through several delivery cycles. A falcon perch above the dock maps the newcomer's payment graph against known clone clusters, and only a cedar register mark—issued after unmatched on-time work—raises its vote weight. Fresh copies never wait out that delay, so they cannot cheaply outvote established workers.
